thread:
marco_garcia: FYI — Julia's team at ParkApps wants a Dedicated pool POC. Their security team requires static egress IPs so they can allowlist on their firewall. Can we do that for a short POC and what do we need from them?

anya_seidel: Yep — two options: (1) Managed static egress for the Dedicated pool (we assign a small set of static IPs per pool) or (2) Private/VPC networking (peer or private wiring) if they need tighter control. For a quick POC, managed static egress is fastest. :thumbsup:

julia_park-customer: timeline is tight — they want to start tests next week. How many IPs will you give and any config we need to send to our infra team?

samir_khan: Technical details: we expose the inference API via TLS on 443. For managed static egress we provide up to 5 IPv4 addresses per pool (can request more as an add-on). They need to allow outbound HTTPS (443) from their VMs to those IPs. We do TLS pass-through; we do not terminate customer TLS inside their network. Recommended allowlist: the exact IPs we provide + the FQDN for redundancy (e.g., api.redwood-inference.com).

marco_garcia: Quick cost note for sales — managed egress is an add-on on top of Dedicated commit. Typical POC concession: waive first-month fee for managed-egress. Check with AMs.

anya_seidel: What we need from ParkApps to provision: 1) Pool size estimate (qps/latency targets), 2) Desired region (us-west-2 or eu-west-1), 3) Contact for firewall changes (name/email), 4) Any upstream proxy/NAT details (if they're egressing through a corporate proxy). Also ask them to sign the standard network enablement form (we'll provide link).

samir_khan: Implementation steps for engineering/networking:
```
- Create Dedicated pool (region X)
- Enable managed static egress flag on pool
- Assign IP set (up to 5 IPs by default)
- Share IPs and FQDN with customer for allowlist
- Monitor flows and open NET ticket for additional IPs if needed
```

samir_khan: Practical notes: if customer has strict outbound rules (only specific ports + IPs allowed), they must allow TLS to our IPs and ALPN h2. If they do deep packet inspection, we recommend a test window and a fallback plan (we can do short-lived private wiring but that takes longer).

julia_park-customer: Can you paste an exact example for our firewall team? They asked for an ACL snippet.

anya_seidel: Example ACL (ask them to adapt to vendor):
```
allow tcp from internal-subnet to 52.14.234.22 port 443 description "Redwood inference managed egress"
allow tcp from internal-subnet to api.redwood-inference.com port 443 description "Redwood FQDN (preferred)"
```

samir_khan: Also include this in the ticket: pool_id (once created), region, desired concurrency, and whether they want reserved or burst capacity. We'll also note that some customers prefer FQDN-based allowlisting, but many corporate firewalls require IPs.

marco_garcia: I'll start the sales enablement thread with AM/finance on pricing and concession. Julia, I'll create the provisioning request after you confirm region + contact.

deploy-bot: NET-REQ-2781 created: "Managed-egress provisioning for pool (ParkApps POC)" — assigned to netops. ETA initial IPs: 24-48h.

julia_park-customer: Confirmed region: us-west-2. Contact: ashley@parkapps.io. Pool estimate: 50 qps, low latency. Thanks — please proceed.

anya_seidel: Great. I'll attach the network enablement form and ask netops to include IPs + any special routing notes. Will follow up in the ticket and loop you in. :rocket:
